chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Allow the hot [food] to cool down, for hot food was brought near the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Allow it until it cools down. It was not for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to feed us the fire, and the blessing is in the cooled [food].'
ai.seo_question: What is the religious etiquette regarding eating hot food according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a prophetic etiquette (adab) for dining, linking physical comfort with spiritual blessing (barakah) by avoiding the consumption of excessively hot food. It highlights the continuity of practice between the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali (AS), framing the cooling of food as a recognition that divine sustenance is meant for human comfort rather than the intensity of fire. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing bodily health with spiritual mindfulness in daily acts of worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allow the heat until it cools down, for hot food was brought near Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allow it until it cools down, it was not for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to feed us the fire, and the Blessings are in the cooled (food)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,

’Leave the hot (food) until it becomes cold. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once was given hot food and he (the Messenger of Allah) said, “Leave it until it becomes cold. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is not the one to feed us fire; the blessing is in the cold.’””
